answer: Each identity owns one quill that writes a single signed note per epoch, and the note must build on a stranger's note from the last epoch, adding one new idea. Good notes send a ripple outward: strangers cite them, and each citation earns the author. Each identity sits at one vertex of a public citation graph, and a note that copies another earns no citation at all. A farm must therefore write a hundred genuinely new, citable notes every epoch, one per vertex, because ink cannot be shared between clones and a copied note is worth nothing.
